title: About Proud Tek — RFID & NFC Manufacturer since 2008
summary: Shenzhen Proud Tek Co., Ltd is a Shenzhen-based RFID and NFC manufacturing partner serving B2B procurement programmes worldwide. Since 2008 we have supplied RFID and NFC credentials directly to B2B buyers: we own the specification, chip sourcing, encoding specification, quality control and compliance documentation, and tooling and production run on contracted partner lines in Shenzhen to our spec. We sell to system integrators, OEMs, hospitality groups, industrial laundries, brand owners and event organisers who need a chip-agnostic partner with traceable quality and predictable lead times.
heroPoints: Manufacturing partner in Shenzhen since 2008 — specification, chip sourcing, encoding spec and QC owned by our own team; tooling and production on contracted partner lines.
Chip-vendor agnostic: NXP, Infineon, Impinj, Alien, EM Microelectronic, Quanray families all supported.

ISO 9001:2015, 14001:2015 and 45001:2018 certified sales and supplier-management operation; OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 on our UHF laundry tag; sample-based RoHS, REACH SVHC and CE test reports published with certificate numbers.

sections.title: Manufacturer-direct vs trading-company sourcing
sections.intro: Most international RFID buyers have been burned at least once by a trading company that re-sold someone else's inlay at a 20-30% markup, with no real engineering support when a deployment ran into reader-range or compliance trouble. The decision to source directly from the manufacturing partner that owns the specification, the chip sourcing and the QC sign-off — rather than from a desk that forwards your PO — is the single biggest cost-and-quality lever you have.

image.alt: Diagram contrasting two sourcing routes: the trading-company route adds a middleman and a 15 to 30 percent markup with no engineering escalation, while buying directly from Proud Tek keeps the margin and routes engineering to the team that built the SKU.

before: One or two middlemen taking 15-30% margin on top of the factory price.
Limited product range; the trading company resells whatever a few partner factories produce.
No engineering escalation path when reader range, anti-collision or chip-side issues appear.
Compliance docs (RoHS, REACH, FCC, CE) charged as extras or simply unavailable.
Lead times depend on the trading company's own queue with their suppliers.
after: Factory pricing direct — full margin stays with you, not a middle layer.
Six product families and the major chip vendors all under one specification and one QC sign-off.
Engineering escalation routed straight to the inlay or encoding team that built the SKU.
ISO 9001 quality system; compliance declarations included with every shipment.
Production schedule visibility; safety-stock arrangements for distributor programs.

sections.title: What we own, and what runs on partner lines
sections.intro: Proud Tek owns the product and antenna specification, chip sourcing through authorised distribution, first-article approval, incoming / in-process / final quality control and export packing. Tooling, lamination and inlay conversion, printing and encoding run on contracted partner lines in Shenzhen to our process specification. Two things never leave our hands: the QC sign-off on every batch and the compliance documentation — those decide whether a programme survives a customs audit or a brand-owner inspection. The step-by-step split is on the [production page](/about/factory/).

image.alt: Six production steps on our partner lines in sequence: inlay bonding, lamination, encoding, one hundred percent read-test QC, laser numbering, and pack and dispatch — with a documented test report shipped per order.

features.title: Wet-inlay assembly
features.text: Chip bonding to PET / PI antennas on our partner lines, to our specification, supporting NXP, Infineon, Impinj, Alien, EM and Quanray families. We are not locked to a single chip vendor.

features.title: Card and label lamination
features.text: PVC, ABS, PETG, recycled-PVC and FSC-certified paper substrates laminated on partner lines to our process spec. Anti-metal ferrite-backed inlays for on-metal asset tagging.

features.title: Encoding and personalization
features.text: UID locking, NDEF programming, GS1 SGTIN-96 encoding, custom block writes, key diversification (MIFARE Plus / DESFire / NTAG 424 DNA) — encoded on the partner line to our encoding specification and read/write verified before shipment.

features.title: Print and marking
features.text: Four-colour offset, screen printing, hot stamping, laser engraving and variable-data inkjet on partner lines against Proud Tek-approved artwork — including consecutive serialisation and QR / barcode overlays.

features.title: Quality control
features.text: Every incoming chip batch read-tested at the reel; every finished batch 100% inspected — chip read/write, print, dimensions, packaging — and signed off by Proud Tek QC. Documented test reports per shipment.

features.title: Packaging and logistics
features.text: Bulk poly bags, individual sleeves, retail blister, custom branded boxes. DHL / FedEx / EMS air freight; sea freight LCL or FCL for distributor volume.

sections.title: Working with Proud Tek — the procurement workflow
sections.intro: Most buyers move from first inquiry to first production order in three to six weeks, depending on whether samples need to clear an internal test phase. The path below describes how a typical RFID OEM program runs with us.

items.label: Step 1 — Inquiry and scoping
items.text: Send us your application context: chip family or read requirements, form factor, environment (on-metal, outdoor, high-temperature, laundry), expected annual volume and any compliance constraints. We reply within 2-4 hours in Shenzhen business hours (Mon-Fri, GMT+8) with a recommended SKU shortlist and indicative pricing.

items.label: Step 2 — Sample qualification
items.text: We propose a free sample set — typically 5–20 pieces across 2–3 SKUs, larger evaluation kits for qualified pilots — prepared in 1 business day; you cover DHL/FedEx freight ($25–60), refunded against your first production order. Most teams take one to two weeks to validate against their reader fleet and integration software.

items.label: Step 3 — Pilot order
items.text: A pilot batch of 200–2,000 pieces validates production quality before the bulk commitment. We lock the encoding scheme, packaging spec and compliance documentation pack; pilot batches ship in 7–15 business days once artwork and encoding files are signed off.

items.label: Step 4 — Production rollout and reorder cadence
items.text: Recurring orders move onto a forecast-based safety-stock program; distributors typically run scheduled call-offs from a 30-90 day buffer at our warehouse. Same account engineer stays on the program across years.

sections.title: Compliance and documentation
sections.intro: Compliance documentation is part of the deliverable, not an upcharge. Every shipment goes out with the documentation buyers need; the certificate numbers below are published on the [certifications page](/about/certifications/) with issuer, scope and validity, and testing on your exact specification (TÜV, SGS, Intertek or the labs named there) can be commissioned when a programme requires it.
bullets: Air-interface standards: ISO/IEC 14443 Type A/B (HF), ISO/IEC 15693 (vicinity), ISO/IEC 18000-6C (UHF EPC Gen2/Gen2v2).

Materials: sample-based RoHS 2.0 certificate of compliance (XKS2025R01150076, RFID card) and REACH SVHC screening of 250 substances (XKS2025R10150032E, RFID keyfob) — they evidence the tested articles; request testing on your own specification for a project-critical file.

Radio / EMF: EN 62311 RF-exposure test report BCTC2509165308-1E on an RFID card; CE marking remains a manufacturer declaration supported by reports like this. Passive tags generally need no radio-type approval — reader devices are approved per device per market.

Management systems: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 (Anhui Certification and Inspection Co., Ltd) over the sales and supplier-management operation; production runs on contracted partner lines.
Skin-contact textile safety: OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 certificate 23.HCN.97349 (Hohenstein), product class II, for our UHF laundry tag.
Sustainability: recycled-PVC stocks and FSC-certified paper labels available on request, with chain-of-custody documents supplied per order.
EU regulatory readiness: EU Digital Product Passport (DPP) compatible inlays, Battery Regulation 2023/1542 traceability files.

callout.label: Note for buyers with specific certification needs
callout.text: If your program requires a specific third-party certification (UL, TÜV, BSCI, Sedex, ISO 27001, etc.) we can route the audit and absorb the documentation cost as part of an annual-volume agreement. Mention it on the initial inquiry so we can scope it from day one.

faq.question: Are you a manufacturer or a trading company?
faq.answer: Neither in the usual sense. Shenzhen Proud Tek Co., Ltd is a manufacturing partner: we own the product and antenna specification, source the chips through authorised distribution, approve the first article, run incoming, in-process and final quality control and manage export packing. Tooling, lamination, printing and encoding are executed on contracted partner lines in Shenzhen to our specification. Unlike a trading company we do not resell someone else's stock product — your order is built to our spec, on lines we hold capacity on, and released only after our QC signs it off. The step-by-step split is on the production page.

faq.question: How long has Proud Tek been operating?
faq.answer: We were founded in 2008 in Shenzhen and have operated continuously since then. We have shipped to customers in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East during that time.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity?
faq.answer: MOQ starts at 500 pieces for cards, keyfobs and wristbands and 1,000 pieces for tags and labels; stock SKUs ship from 100 pieces, UHF inlays and labels on reel stock from 5,000, and formats that need custom tooling 2,000-5,000. For a locked SKU the MOQ halves after the first three orders. Free samples and pilot batches of 200-2,000 pieces are available before you commit.

faq.question: How does pricing work — do you publish a price list?
faq.answer: Product pages show indicative FOB Shenzhen price ranges (dated Q3 2026) so you can budget before you talk to us; the firm price depends on chip allocation, antenna size, encoding scope and order volume. Send a target SKU, expected annual volume and packaging requirement: first reply within 2-4 hours in Shenzhen business hours, itemised written quotation within 24-48 hours, valid 30 days.

faq.question: What lead times should we plan around?
faq.answer: Standard production ships in 7-15 business days from order confirmation for stock chip types; custom tooling or new-antenna programmes are quoted per job and typically run 8-10 weeks end to end. Pilot batches of 200-2,000 pieces ship in 7-15 business days, repeat orders on a framework agreement in 10-12, and distributors on safety-stock programmes see call-off shipments within 3-5 business days of release authorisation.

faq.question: Which chip families do you support?
faq.answer: We are chip-vendor agnostic. Current inventory covers NXP (MIFARE Classic / Plus / DESFire / NTAG 213/215/216/424 DNA / ICODE SLIX / UCODE 8/9), Infineon (My-d / NEO), Impinj (Monza 4/R6/R6-P/M7xx), Alien (Higgs-3/4/9/EC), EM Microelectronic (EM4200/4305/4423) and T5577 LF families. If your program needs a chip we do not stock, we will requisition it through the manufacturer's authorized distribution channel.

faq.question: Can you support EU Digital Product Passport and Battery Regulation programs?
faq.answer: Yes. Our NFC NTAG 213/215/216/424 DNA and UHF UCODE 8/9 inlays meet the air-interface and memory requirements for EU DPP (ESPR / Regulation 2024/1781). We supply the technical files needed for Battery Regulation 2023/1542 traceability as part of the standard documentation pack.

faq.question: Do you have a US, EU or UK office?
faq.answer: Proud Tek is operated out of Shenzhen with no overseas office. We work with buyers globally in English, with Chinese, Spanish and Arabic available on request. Local logistics is handled through DHL, FedEx and EMS partners; sea-freight LCL / FCL arrangements use standard FOB Shenzhen / Yantian incoterms.

faq.question: What payment terms are available?
faq.answer: Standard terms are 30% T/T deposit, 70% balance before shipment. L/C at sight or 50/50 terms are available for established accounts, and PayPal is accepted for sample orders under $500. We do not require Western Union or personal-account payment routes.
